lines.text: In this lesson, you will learn to use broadcasts and variables to add a start screen, levels and a game-over state to a game.
A game is in different states: a start menu, playing, the next level, game over.
Code needs to know which state it is in.
When the player presses space on the menu, broadcast start.
Every sprite that needs to begin listens for “when I receive start”.
A level variable remembers how far the player is.
When the score reaches a target, change the level, switch the backdrop and make it harder.
When lives reach 0 or time runs out, broadcast game over: show the final score and stop all.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
